messages.author: fc7cc12862219cdf
messages.subject: Construction habitat mask : poly argument
parts:
Hello,

I'm working on a SCR on Balkan lynx and I have some troubles to construct the habitat mask. I would like to exclude areas of non-habitat i.e. above 1800m of elevation and water bodies. I tried to construct this polygon on QGIS or R but I have the same problems for both. The rings in the polygon seem to be the problem. In a previous SCR analysis I managed to solve this by creating a "channel" from the ring to outside the buffer. But here there is too many rings and not close to the edge of the buffer. Maybe it's more a question about GIS, just tell me if it's the case !

All the shapefiles in the folder use the EPSG WGS84. I also attached a JPEG of the mask.

My script :
library(rgdal)
library(raster)
library(tidyr)

TDF = read.csv('Traps2018_60occ.csv', sep=';')
trapfile = read.traps(data=TDF, detector="count")
usage(trapfile) = TDF[,c(4:63)]

water = as(readOGR(layer='water_bodies', dsn="...", verbose = FALSE), 'SpatialPolygons')
ele = as(readOGR(layer='ISO_1800', dsn="...", verbose = FALSE), 'SpatialPolygons')
buf = as(readOGR(layer='Buffer_2018', dsn="...", verbose = FALSE), 'SpatialPolygons')
plot(buf)
plot(water)
plot(ele)
habit = erase(buf, water)
plot(habit)
habit = erase(habit, ele)
plot(habit)
#OR WITH LAYER CREATED ON GIS
habit = readOGR(layer='suitable_habitat2018', dsn="...", verbose = FALSE)
#THEN
habit.UTM <- spTransform(habit, CRS("+init=epsg:32634"))
cord.habit.UTM = SpatialPoints(cbind(tidy(habit.UTM)$long, tidy(habit.UTM)$lat), proj4string = CRS("+init=epsg:32634"))
habit.poly = data.frame(cord.habit.UTM)

mask = make.mask(trapfile, 
                 buffer = 23000, 
                 spacing = 1900, 
                 type ="trapbuffer",
                 poly = habit.poly) 
plot(mask)

Thank you !

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Construction habitat mask : poly argument
parts:
Hi
I can't track this down as I don't have the data sources, and yes this is a GIS problem that is probably out of my league, but...
make.mask() uses pointsInPolygon() that uses sp::over (xy, poly). So you can troubleshoot by constructing a matrix xy (essentially the unfiltered mask) and applying that either pointsInPolygon or sp::over.
Murray

messages.subject: Re: Habitat mask : poly argument
parts:
Hi,
Thank you Murray ! I managed to do it as you said using over. My script if it can be useful for anyone :

habit2018 = readOGR(layer='suitable_habitat2018_ele+wat', dsn="D:/Users/yonha/Documents/Stage MES/Carto/LynxSCR", verbose = FALSE)
habit2018.UTM = spTransform(habit2018, CRS("+init=epsg:32634"))

mask2018 = make.mask(TF2018, 
                 buffer = 23000, 
                 spacing = 1700, 
                 type ="trapbuffer")

mask_pts = SpatialPoints(coords = cbind (mask2018$x, mask2018$y), proj4string =  CRS("+init=epsg:32634"))
mask2018_habitat = as.data.frame(mask_pts[habit2018.UTM])
mask2018 = read.mask(data = mask2018_habitat)

By the way, the data sources were :
- For area above 1800m of elevation : DEM -> level curves -> lines to polygon 
- For water bodies : Open Street Map 

And now that I managed to exclude non habitat areas, I wonder if it's correct to create session specific masks with different buffer widths and spacings (not only trap locations). Because if I do again all the process to choose the buffer width (and therefore the spacing) for each session, it's absolutely not the same for one of the three sessions (much smaller). Maybe I have to keep the larger buffer width...
If it's correct, can I compute it like this :

D.ss.sig.sex = secr.fit(capturedata, model=list(D ~ session, g0 ~ 1, sigma ~ h2), hcov ='sex', mask = list(mask2013, mask2015, mask2018), detectfn = 0) 
No warnings at the end :-)

Thank you !
